source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Uncomplicated dyspepsia, because sudden severe pain and a rigid abdomen are expected findings during a routine peptic-ulcer flare.","B":"Perforated peptic ulcer with peritonitis and peritoneal signs, a surgical emergency requiring immediate evaluation and management.","C":"Simple constipation, because a board-like abdomen most often reflects stool retention rather than peritoneal irritation.","D":"Musculoskeletal abdominal-wall pain, because ulcer complications do not typically cause abrupt severe pain or guarding."}}
source_row.rationale: Sudden, severe, sharp abdominal pain with a rigid, board-like abdomen in a client with known peptic ulcer disease is highly concerning for ulcer perforation, a surgical emergency (leading to peritonitis) requiring immediate provider notification and evaluation, distinct from typical, more gradual ulcer-related discomfort.
source_row.source_detail: WSES PPU guideline, Diagnosis section: perforation usually presents with sudden abdominal pain and localized/generalized peritonitis; CT is recommended for suspected perforated peptic ulcer. World J Emerg Surg 2020;15:3, DOI 10.1186/s13017-019-0283-9; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
